full_judgment:
Naima Haider J: Both these petitions, being Transfer Petition Nos. 1 and 2 of 2013 have been filed under Article 110 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh to transfer the suits, being Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2012 and Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 2012, to an appropriate Bench of the High Court Division of Supreme Court of Bangladesh from the District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manikganj. Since both these transfer petitions involve common question of fact and law we are inclined to deal with both the petitions by this single judgment. 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why an order, pursuant to Article 110 of the Constitution, should not be issued to withdraw Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2012 now pending in the District Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manikganj and transfer the same to an appropriate Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division, which may he constituted for this purpose for trial and disposal of the same and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper" 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why an order, pursuant to Article 110 of the Constitution, should not be issued to withdraw Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 2012 now pending in the District Judge & Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manikganj and transfer the same to an appropriate Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division, which may be constituted for this purpose for trial and disposal of the same and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper" 

 5. Subsequent to the accident on 13-8-2011 Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2012 and Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2012 were filed under Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1983 ("the 1983 Ordinance") and damages were sought. The damages were claimed under different heads, including loss of dependency, loss of income and loss of estate, loss of love and affection, funeral expenses, expenses for repairing damaged vehicle, medical expenses, resulting from the said incident. We also note that "exemplary damages" were sought as well. The heads of damages, it seems, are purely tortious. While claims under tort are common in many jurisdictions, the position in Bangladesh is rather different. 

 6. We note from the records that the aforesaid miscellaneous cases were contested by filing their respective written statements. The respondents have stated their version of what caused the unfortunate and tragic accident. We are not inclined to discuss these facts since any discussion from our end may affect the merits of the suits. 

 7. The plaintiffs in the aforesaid miscellaneous cases, as petitioners filed these transfer petitions under Article 110 of the Constitution to withdraw the aforesaid miscellaneous cases from the learned District Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manikgonj and to transfer the same to an appropriate Bench of this Division for trial and disposal. The petitioners contend that the transfer petitions were filed since certain substantial questions of law and point of general public importance having arisen, which include: 

 8. Dr Kamal Hossain, Senior Advocate representing the petitioners draws our attention to Article 110 of the Constitution which empowers the High Court Division to withdraw any case pending before any subordinate court, if the case involves substantial question of law or involves a point of general public importance. Relevant part of Article 110 of the Constitution, upon which Dr. Hossain places so much emphasis is set out below: 

 "110. If the High Court Division is satisfied that a case pending in a court subordinate to it involves a substantial Question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, or on a point of general public importance.the determination of which is necessary for the disposal of the case, it shall withdraw the case from that court and may- 

 (a) Either let disposal of the case by itself; or 

 9. Having reviewed. Article 110 of the Constitution, we feel that while the Constitution empowers this Division to assume jurisdiction over matters pending before any subordinate court, the Constitution also envisaged that this Division should be extremely careful in exercising the powers under Article 110. This Division Bench must not be eager to exercise jurisdiction on matters pending before any subordinate court just because there is an interesting issue arising out of a case. This Division should exercise the power to withdraw a case from a competent court only if that particular case gives rise to substantial question of law or if the case involves point of public importance. Our understanding of Article 110 of the Constitution is that we should be very slow in exercising the powers conferred therein because of the constitutional limitations. 

 10. The respondent No.5-Reliance Insurance Limited filed an Affidavit-in-Opposition in which it is stated that the miscellaneous cases should not be transferred in exercise of the powers under Article 110 of the Constitution since: 

 (b) Disposal of the miscellaneous cases is not matter of general public importance, rather disposal of the said cases will only benefit the parties concerned; 

 (c) The petitioners are praying for interpretation of a statutory provision of section 130 of  Vehicles Ordinance, 1983 and such interpretation is not a ground for transfer of cases under Article 110 of the Constitution; 

 13. We have taken a note of the points raised by Dr. Hossain. We asked ourselves whether the Constitution mandates "unfettered discretionary powers" to any court including this Division Bench. We also asked ourselves whether it is possible, within the existing constitutional scheme, to refuse "right of representation" in a case where a person is claiming damages for the loss suffered. 

 14. In our opinion, "right of representation" is fundamental to a fair trial and that if any court is empowered to refuse such right, then court should be very careful in refusing the right and should be appropriately guided on the circumstances when right representation can be refused under the existing constitutional scheme. We have not seen any such guidance upon the courts from the empowering statute or otherwise. We strongly feel that this Division in the absence of any guidelines being provided by the statute or subordinate legislation on what should be the standard of "fair trial", is constitutionally empowered and mandated to provide appropriate guidance. The only way it seems to us that this Division Bench can provide such guidance is by deciding the miscellaneous cases. 

 16. Dr. Hossain pointed out that the measure of damages in tortious claim is different from the measure of damages arising out of, for instance, contractual claim. Dr. Hossain further pointed out that while the judgments of the apex courts of different jurisdictions, including India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are highly persuasive, without a comprehensive judgment from our apex courts, the subordinate courts feel reluctant to take those into consideration. Under the current trend, the subordinate courts use the judgment of the apex courts of other jurisdiction if the Supreme Court of Bangladesh has reviewed the issue, partly or fully. We agree with his observation. Accordingly, we feel that a comprehensive judgment should come from Supreme Court of Bangladesh which extensively deals with the tortious concept and clarifies how tort laws should be interpreted. We are inclined to take the view that an appropriately empowered Division Bench of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh should show how tortious claim be dealt with. If this is not done, social injustice that we see would not be cured and cases of negligence would go unpunished. We feel time has come for us to recognize the concept of duty of care, the applicable standard of care owed which would be instrumental in determining whether there has been negligence. 

 17. Dr Hossain submitted that through adjudication of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Cases, an appropriately constituted Division Bench may lay down guidelines which could ensure that victims of negligence and their dependents can get just compensation. A salutary result may be that those who are committing negligence now would start to exercise due care. We agree. For that reason, we think that we should intervene. 

 18. We also agree with Dr. Hossain that the issues raised in these cases present an opportunity for consideration of the impact of the fundamental rights provisions of the Constitution, in particular, the right to life (Article 32) and the right to protection of law for life (Article 31), in the case of death caused by negligence or breach of statutory duty and the right to appropriate compensation in such a case. 

 21. We note that the computation of damages claimed by the petitioners have been derived by calculations taking into account the deceased's age, income, assets, dependants and life expectancy. We feel that this Division Bench is in best position to lay down a formula for the computation of damages in these cases and in case of negligence in general, specifying factors which may be taken into account. As stated before, all these can only be done if we allow the instant transfer petitions which would enable an appropriately constituted Bench of this Division, to adjudicate the miscellaneous cases. 

 22. We are unable to agree with Mr Siddique's submission that principles of determination of compensation in tort have been comprehensively settled by our Courts. We are also unable to accept his submission that disposal of the Miscellaneous Cases by the High Court Division will benefit the petitioner only. At the same time, we find it difficult to understand why interpretation of the 1983 Ordinance, in the aforesaid context is not a ground for exercising our powers under Article 110 of the Constitution and why our intervention would "usurp" the authority of Bangladesh Road Transport Authority. However, we fully agree with Mr Siddique that this Bench should be extremely careful in exercising the powers under Article 110 of the Constitution and that only in exceptional circumstances envisaged in the Constitution, the power should be exercised. In view of the aforesaid, we are of the view that: 

 (a) Miscellaneous Cases give rise to both substantial question of law and also involves a point of general public importance: 

 23. We, therefore, hold the view that the submissions advanced by Dr Hossain deserve favourable consideration and accordingly, the rules in both the transfer petitions are made absolute without any order as to costs. We recommend that the miscellaneous cases be referred to an appropriately constituted Bench of this Division. 

 Let the records of the aforesaid miscellaneous cases and the records of the transfer petitions be placed before the Hon'ble Chief Justice so that His Lordship may pass appropriate order relating to constitution of appropriate Bench and/or pass any other orders as His Lordship considers proper.
